message.content:
Civil law—often called **private or non‑criminal law**—regulates relationships between private parties rather than offenses against society. Its core components can be grouped into three broad categories: | Category | Key Elements | |----------|--------------| | **1️⃣ Sources & Foundations** | • Statutory codes (e.g., contracts, torts, property)
• Case law / judicial precedent (especially in common‑law jurisdictions)
• Legal doctrine & scholarly treatises
• Constitutional provisions affecting civil rights | | **2️⃣ Substantive Areas** | • **Contract Law:** formation, performance, breach, remedies.
• **Tort Law:** negligence, intentional wrongs, strict liability; damages.
• **Property/Real Estate Law:** ownership, leasing, easements, mortgages.
• **Family Law:** marriage, divorce, child custody, alimony.
• **Inheritance/Wills:** succession rules, intestate estates.
• **Commercial Law:** company incorporation, securities, bankruptcy.
• **Consumer Protection:** unfair trade practices, warranties.
• **Intellectual Property (in some systems):** patents, trademarks, copyrights. | | **3️⃣ Procedural Mechanisms** | • **Jurisdiction & Venue Rules** – who may hear a claim and where.
• **Pleadings & Discovery** – how claims are presented and evidence gathered.
• **Trial Procedures** – admissibility, burden of proof, evidentiary standards.
• **Remedies & Enforcement** – monetary compensation, injunctions, specific performance, restitution.
• **Appeals Process** – review mechanisms and appellate courts’ role.| ### How It Works Together 1. **Legislation** sets out general rules (codes). 2. **Judicial decisions** interpret those rules, filling gaps and shaping evolving norms. 3. **Procedures** ensure disputes are resolved fairly, efficiently, and consistently across cases. In many modern states, civil law is heavily codified (think Germany’s *Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch* or France’s *Code civil*) but still relies on court interpretations to adapt to new circumstances. In common‑law countries, statutes coexist with rich precedential traditions that guide judges when legislation is silent. --- #### Quick Takeaway Civil law covers all matters involving private individuals or entities—contracts you sign, injuries you suffer, properties you own—and it operates through a blend of written statutes, judge-made rulings, and formal dispute‑resolution processes.
